fields.label: Adequacy
fields.help: Auto reads the aggregate length: good over 20 mm, compromised 10-20 mm, inadequate under 10 mm (RCPath tissue pathways, 2020). Ten or fewer portal tracts under-estimate grade and stage (BSG 2020).

reference.title: Biopsy adequacy
reference.intro: State the core length, fragmentation and an approximate portal-tract count (RCPath G064; BSG 2020).

groups.heading: RCPath tiers (total core length)
points: Good: over 20 mm
Compromised: 10-20 mm
Inadequate: under 10 mm
Trials: at least 20 mm with more than 10 portal tracts per section

images.caption: Three percutaneous needle cores at scanning power (H&E).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 3

groups.heading: Why size matters
points: 10 or fewer portal tracts under-estimate the fibrosis stage and inflammatory grade in chronic viral hepatitis
The portal-tract count cannot be predicted from the length
Transjugular cores (19 G) are narrower and need several passes

fields.label: Pattern
fields.help: Choose the dominant pattern of injury; the fields below follow it.

reference.title: Patterns of injury
reference.intro: Name the pattern first, then the likely cause; RCPath advises against an unqualified "chronic hepatitis" for unexplained portal inflammation.

groups.heading: Hepatitic
points: Portal inflammation with interface and lobular hepatitis
Grade and stage: Ishak, METAVIR or Batts-Ludwig
Causes: AIH, hepatitis B or C, drugs

images.caption: Interface hepatitis: a portal tract whose infiltrate breaches the limiting plate into the adjacent lobule (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: Biliary
points: Duct injury or loss, ductular reaction, periportal copper-associated protein and CK7
PBC: florid duct lesions and granulomas; PSC: periductal concentric fibrosis
Large-duct obstruction: portal oedema, ductular reaction, neutrophils

images.caption: Primary biliary cholangitis: an expanded portal tract with a dense lymphoid infiltrate and a pale epithelioid (granulomatous) area (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Steatotic
points: Steatosis over 5%; steatohepatitis needs ballooning and lobular inflammation
Score with NAS (0-8) and stage with NASH CRN; SAF optional

images.caption: Ballooned hepatocytes with rarefied cytoplasm and Mallory-Denk bodies in steatohepatitis (H&E, x200).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 15

groups.heading: Transplant
points: Banff global assessment with the rejection activity index (RAI, 0-9)
Portal inflammation, bile duct damage and venous endothelial inflammation, each 0-3

groups.heading: Donor (time zero)
points: A donor liver before or soon after implantation, or a living-donor work-up
Large- and small-droplet fat by the Banff three-step method, necrosis, ischaemia-reperfusion injury and fibrosis

groups.heading: Other
points: Granulomas, iron overload, venous outflow obstruction, non-specific reactive change

images.caption: Congestive hepatopathy: perivenular sinusoidal dilatation and congestion (trichrome).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

fields.label: Timing
fields.help: Post-reperfusion biopsies are graded for ischaemia-reperfusion injury; back-table and work-up biopsies are not.

reference.title: Donor liver biopsy, step by step
reference.intro: Ten steps for a time-zero or work-up biopsy (Banff 2022, Clin Transplant Res 2025, AASLD Pathology Pearls, Sabry 2025, CAP). Cut-offs are for the Checks; none of them prints.

groups.heading: 1. Timing and handling
points: Back-table (before implantation), post-reperfusion, or a living-donor work-up biopsy (CAP)
Post-reperfusion biopsies: about 2-3 h after portal reperfusion (Sabry 2025)
Send fresh and quickly; no saline, air drying or absorbent paper (Clin Transplant Res 2025; UCLA)
Cut at 5-6 µm: thinner sections overestimate large-droplet fat (Banff 2022)

groups.heading: 2. Adequacy
points: At least six portal tracts is the common standard (Clin Transplant Res 2025)

groups.heading: 3. Exclude malignancy first
points: It makes the graft unsuitable: tick Neoplasm and give the type in a comment (Clin Transplant Res 2025)

groups.heading: 4. Steatosis, Banff three-step
points: Low power: the share of the area occupied by fat
About x20: the share of hepatocytes in that area with large-droplet fat; their product is the large-droplet %
Small-droplet fat is given on its own and never added; true microvesicular steatosis (foamy cells) is rare and keeps its own term (Banff 2022)

groups.heading: 5. Necrosis
points: Usually focal, in zone 3 or under the capsule; to the nearest 10%, with its site (AASLD)
Address ischaemic necrosis in every deceased donor (Clin Transplant Res 2025)

groups.heading: 6. Ischaemia-reperfusion injury
points: Post-reperfusion only; graded none to severe (Sabry 2025)
Zonal necrosis without neutrophils is donor ischaemia: enter it as necrosis

groups.heading: 7. Inflammation
points: Score portal and lobular inflammation separately
Minimal to mild non-specific inflammation is common; moderate or more suggests underlying disease (AASLD)

groups.heading: 8. Fibrosis
points: Stage as usual, Ishak by default; precise staging needs a trichrome (AASLD; CAP)

groups.heading: 9. Other findings
points: Ballooning, iron (zone 3 suggests overload: add Perls), lipofuscin and cholestasis (Clin Transplant Res 2025)
Granulomas and amyloid (AASLD); alpha-1 antitrypsin globules (Int J Organ Transplant Med 2017)

groups.heading: 10. Baseline for later biopsies
points: Tells preservation-reperfusion injury in the first 1-2 weeks from acute rejection (Int J Organ Transplant Med 2017)
Preservation injury has a less dense infiltrate than TCMR and no endotheliitis (CAP)

reference.note: The Checks flag large-droplet fat of 30% or more (UCLA), over 33% (Clin Transplant Res 2025) and over 60-66% (Banff 2022); fewer than six portal tracts; necrosis of 10% or more, though up to 50% has been used, especially from brain-dead donors; and Ishak stage 2 or more (Clin Transplant Res 2025).

fields.label: Donor type
fields.help: For the Checks only; it does not print.

fields.label: Large-droplet fat (%)
fields.help: Banff three-step: the area occupied by fat at low power, times the share of hepatocytes in it with large droplets at about x20.

fields.label: Small-droplet fat (%)
fields.help: Given on its own; never added to the large-droplet figure.

fields.label: True microvesicular steatosis
fields.help: Foamy hepatocytes with innumerable tiny droplets and a central nucleus; rare, and kept apart from small-droplet fat.

reference.title: Donor steatosis
reference.intro: Give large- and small-droplet fat as separate percentages and never add them (Banff 2022).

groups.heading: Banff three-step method
points: 1. Low power: estimate the share of the area occupied by fat
2. About x20: estimate the share of hepatocytes in that area with large-droplet fat
3. The x20 share of the low-power share is the large-droplet %: 50% of 20% is 10%
Cut at 5-6 µm; thinner sections overestimate large-droplet fat

groups.heading: Droplet type
points: Large droplet: one droplet distends the cell and displaces the nucleus
Small droplet: smaller droplets with a central nucleus; true microvesicular steatosis is foamy cytoplasm, rare, and named apart

images.caption: Microvesicular steatosis in acute fatty liver of pregnancy: foamy hepatocytes (arrows); inset, macrovesicular steatosis for comparison (H&E).
images.credit: Ronen, Shaheen, Steinberg, Justus, Cureus 2018, via Wikimedia Commons

fields.label: Necrosis (%)
fields.help: To the nearest 10%; usually zone 3 or subcapsular. Address it in every deceased donor.

fields.label: Ischaemia-reperfusion injury
fields.help: Sabry 2025 grades. Zonal necrosis without neutrophils is donor ischaemia: enter it as necrosis.

reference.title: Ischaemia-reperfusion injury at time zero
reference.intro: Grades from Sabry 2025, for post-reperfusion biopsies only.

groups.heading: Grades (Sabry 2025)
points: None
Minimal: sparse single sinusoidal neutrophils, no hepatocyte loss
Mild: sporadic hepatocyte detachment or acidophil bodies, with isolated neutrophils
Moderate: clusters of more than five neutrophils, with or without hepatocyte loss
Severe: zonal or confluent, usually perivenular, hepatocyte loss

groups.heading: Preservation-reperfusion injury
points: Zone 3 hepatocyte swelling, apoptosis, cholestasis and sinusoidal neutrophil clusters
Usually mild and resolving within 1-2 weeks; compare with the time-zero biopsy

images.caption: Time-zero biopsy: moderate ischaemia-reperfusion injury with clusters of more than 5 neutrophils and hepatocyte dropout (x200).
images.credit: Sabry et al., Int J Hepatol 2025, Fig 4

fields.label: Other findings
fields.help: Exclude malignancy first; give the type of any neoplasm in a comment. Iron is the Perls fields under Stains.

reference.title: Inflammation
reference.intro: Grade portal, interface and lobular inflammation separately, then name the predominant cell type; the cell type narrows the differential more than the grade does.

groups.heading: Portal inflammation
points: Minimal to marked; say whether some or most portal tracts are involved (Ishak D)
Lymphoid aggregates in a lymphocytic portal infiltrate are common in hepatitis C

images.caption: Portal inflammation: a portal tract expanded by a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in autoimmune hepatitis (H&E, low power).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Interface hepatitis
points: Lymphocytes and plasma cells cross the limiting plate and surround periportal hepatocytes
Ishak A: focal or continuous, around fewer or more than half of the tracts or septa

images.caption: Interface hepatitis at high power: lymphocytes surrounding periportal hepatocytes at the edge of a portal tract (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: Lobular inflammation
points: Count foci of necro-inflammation per 10x objective field (Ishak C)
Spotty necrosis: focal hepatocyte dropout with lymphocytes; note confluent necrosis separately (Ishak B)

images.caption: Lobular necro-inflammation: scattered small clusters of lymphocytes and histiocytes within the lobule (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Spotty (focal) necrosis: focal hepatocyte dropout accompanied by lymphocytes (H&E, x200).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 9

groups.heading: Infiltrate type
points: Plasma cells and clusters of 5 or more: AIH; in an allograft, plasma cell-rich rejection
Eosinophils: drug injury; with oedema and endothelial swelling in an allograft, consider AMR
Neutrophils: large-duct obstruction; within ducts and lumina, ascending cholangitis

images.caption: Plasma cell-rich infiltrate: lymphocytes and plasma cells at the portal-lobular interface in autoimmune hepatitis (H&E, high power).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons

reference.title: Hepatitis
reference.intro: Describe the pattern first, then the cause the morphology supports; AIH and drug injury are clinicopathological diagnoses (IAIHG 2022; RCPath G064).

groups.heading: Autoimmune hepatitis
points: Portal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with interface and lobular hepatitis
IAIHG 2022: likely, possible or unlikely; rosettes and emperipolesis are descriptive only

images.caption: Autoimmune hepatitis: a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate at the interface between a portal tract and the hepatocytes (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Chronic hepatitis B and C
points: B: ground-glass hepatocytes, confirmed with HBsAg; C: lymphocytic portal infiltrate, often with lymphoid aggregates
Grade and stage with Ishak, METAVIR or Batts-Ludwig

images.caption: Ground-glass hepatocytes with finely granular pale cytoplasm in chronic hepatitis B (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Drug-induced liver injury
points: Hepatitic, cholestatic or mixed; eosinophils and granulomas go with milder injury
Necrosis, fibrosis, microvesicular steatosis and ductular reaction go with more severe injury

images.caption: Drug-induced hepatitis: a small non-caseating epithelioid granuloma in the lobule (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

images.caption: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) toxicity: zone 3 submassive necrosis (H&E, x40).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 11

groups.heading: Acute hepatitis
points: Lobular disarray with lymphocytic inflammation, acidophil bodies and bilirubinostasis
Causes include viral hepatitis, drugs and acute-onset AIH

images.caption: Acute hepatitis: lobular disarray with lymphocytic inflammation, an acidophil body (arrow) and bilirubinostasis (H&E).
images.credit: Boyd, Cain, Chauhan, Webb, Frontline Gastroenterol 2020, via Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: Necrosis patterns
points: Spotty, confluent, bridging, submassive or massive; state the zone
Zone 3 necrosis with little inflammation suggests ischaemia or paracetamol

images.caption: Ischaemic (shock) liver: centrilobular necrosis with viable periportal hepatocytes (H&E, annotated).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Massive hepatic necrosis in hepatitis B: hepatocyte dropout with residual hepatocytes and an intact portal framework (H&E, x100).
images.credit: Xue, Zhu, Liu, Meng, Sci Rep 2019, via Wikimedia Commons

fields.label: DILI pattern
fields.help: DILIN hepatocellular patterns (Kleiner 2014); the cholestatic patterns sit under Biliary.

fields.label: AIH histology category
fields.help: IAIHG 2022 (portal pattern): likely = portal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with more than mild interface or lobular hepatitis and no features of another disease. 2008: typical needs interface hepatitis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, emperipolesis and rosettes.

reference.title: Ishak modified HAI
reference.intro: Grade = A + B + C + D (0-18). For autoimmune hepatitis IAIHG 2022 uses A + B + C only (0-14).

groups.heading: A - interface hepatitis (0-4)
points: 0 absent
1 mild: focal, few portal areas
2 mild/moderate: focal, most portal areas
3 moderate: continuous around under 50% of tracts or septa
4 severe: continuous around over 50%

images.caption: Interface hepatitis: inflammation at the limiting plate around more than half of a portal tract (H&E, x100).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 8

groups.heading: B - confluent necrosis (0-6)
points: 0 absent
1 focal confluent necrosis
2 zone 3 necrosis in some areas
3 zone 3 necrosis in most areas
4 zone 3 necrosis with occasional portal-central bridging
5 zone 3 necrosis with multiple portal-central bridging
6 panacinar or multiacinar necrosis

images.caption: Bridging necrosis: hepatocyte loss and inflammation extending between portal tracts (H&E, x100).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 10

groups.heading: C and D (0-4 each)
points: C focal lytic necrosis, apoptosis and focal inflammation per 10x objective: 0 absent, 1 one focus or fewer, 2 two to four, 3 five to ten, 4 more than ten
D portal inflammation: 0 none, 1 mild (some or all), 2 moderate (some or all), 3 moderate/marked (all), 4 marked (all)

fields.label: METAVIR activity
fields.help: Auto derives A from piecemeal and lobular necrosis (Bedossa 1996 algorithm).

optionLabels.Chronic biliary disease: Chronic biliary disease, cause not stated

reference.title: Biliary disease
reference.intro: Look at every portal tract for duct injury or loss, then for the periportal changes of chronic cholestasis: ductular reaction, copper-associated protein and CK7 (RCPath G064).

groups.heading: Primary biliary cholangitis
points: Florid duct lesion: lymphocytes within the duct epithelium, often with epithelioid granulomas
Mixed portal infiltrate; stage with Nakanuma (orcein for copper-associated protein)

images.caption: Primary biliary cholangitis: a damaged bile duct with intraepithelial lymphocytes in a mixed portal infiltrate, with a poorly formed granuloma nearby (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
points: Concentric periductal (onion-skin) fibrosis; fibro-obliterative scars are seen in a minority of biopsies
Often only non-specific chronic biliary features on a needle core; imaging decides

images.caption: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: a bile duct surrounded by concentric periductal (onion-skin) fibrosis (H&E).
images.credit: Worthington, Chapman, Orphanet J Rare Dis 2006, Fig 2 (cropped)

groups.heading: Large-duct obstruction
points: Portal oedema, ductular reaction at the limiting plate and focal neutrophils
Neutrophils within ducts and lumina raise ascending cholangitis

images.caption: Large-duct obstruction: an oedematous portal tract with neutrophils and reactive bile duct epithelium (H&E).
images.credit: Vaz, J Med Case Rep 2019, Fig 2

groups.heading: Cholestasis
points: Hepatocellular and canalicular bile, maximal in zone 3
Periportal cholate stasis (feathery change, Mallory-Denk bodies) means chronic cholestasis

images.caption: Cholestasis: bile pigment in hepatocytes and dilated canaliculi (H&E, high power).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons

reference.title: Cholestatic drug injury
reference.intro: Drugs are the commonest cause of bland cholestasis; the differential includes early large-duct obstruction, sepsis and occult lymphoma (RCPath G064).

groups.heading: Bland cholestasis
points: Canalicular bile plugs with little inflammation or hepatocyte injury

images.caption: Bland canalicular cholestasis without significant inflammation in drug-induced liver injury (H&E, x400).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 18

groups.heading: Features favouring drug over AIH
points: Hepatocellular pattern: intra-acinar eosinophils, canalicular cholestasis
Cholestatic pattern: portal neutrophils, hepatocellular cholestasis (Suzuki 2011)

fields.label: Portal tracts without a bile duct

reference.title: Nakanuma staging (PBC)
reference.intro: Stage from the sum of fibrosis, bile duct loss and orcein-positive granules (0-9), or of fibrosis and duct loss alone (0-6) when orcein is not assessed (Nakanuma 2010).

groups.heading: Items (0-3 each)
points: Fibrosis: 0 none or portal only; 1 periportal or incomplete septal; 2 bridging; 3 cirrhosis
Bile duct loss: 0 none; 1 under 1/3 of tracts; 2 1/3-2/3; 3 over 2/3
Orcein granules: 0 none; 1 several periportal cells in under 1/3 of tracts; 2 1/3-2/3; 3 many cells in over 2/3

images.caption: Primary biliary cholangitis: an expanded portal tract with a dense lymphoid infiltrate and a pale epithelioid (granulomatous) area (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Stage
points: With orcein: 0 stage 1; 1-3 stage 2; 4-6 stage 3; 7-9 stage 4
Without orcein: 0 stage 1; 1-2 stage 2; 3-4 stage 3; 5-6 stage 4
Stage 1 no, 2 mild, 3 moderate, 4 advanced progression

images.caption: Copper in periportal hepatocytes as coarse orange-brown granules (rhodanine, x200); here Wilson disease.
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 20

groups.heading: Activity (revised)
points: CA1 one duct with evident chronic cholangitis; CA2 more than two; CA3 at least one CNSDC (includes granulomatous cholangitis)
HA1-HA3 interface hepatitis of 10 continuous hepatocytes in one tract, in more than two, or of 20 in over half, with lobular hepatitis

images.caption: Ductular reaction around the native bile duct (BD) (CK7, x200).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 17

optionLabels.1: 1 - one duct with evident chronic cholangitis

reference.title: Steatosis and steatohepatitis
reference.intro: Grade steatosis on the whole core, then look for ballooning and lobular inflammation; steatohepatitis needs both, and the NAS does not replace that judgement (Kleiner 2005).

groups.heading: Steatosis grade
points: 0 under 5%; 1 5-33%; 2 over 33-66%; 3 over 66% of parenchyma (NASH CRN)
SAF counts large and medium droplets only, not foamy microvesicles

images.caption: Steatosis grades in chronic hepatitis B: (a) none, (b) mild, (c) moderate and (d) severe (H&E, x200).
images.credit: Zhang, Wang, Kang, Wu, Wang, Sci Rep 2016, via Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: Droplet type
points: Macrovesicular: one large droplet displaces the nucleus
Microvesicular: foamy cytoplasm with a central nucleus; report it separately

images.caption: Microvesicular steatosis in acute fatty liver of pregnancy: foamy hepatocytes (arrows); inset, macrovesicular steatosis for comparison (H&E).
images.credit: Ronen, Shaheen, Steinberg, Justus, Cureus 2018, via Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: Ballooning and Mallory-Denk bodies
points: Ballooning: rounded pale, reticulated cells; grade 2 when some are at least twice normal size (SAF)
Mallory-Denk bodies: ropy eosinophilic inclusions, often in ballooned cells; not specific

images.caption: A ballooned hepatocyte in steatohepatitis: cell enlargement with reticulated cytoplasm (H&E, annotated).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Mallory-Denk body (circled): a ropy eosinophilic inclusion in a hepatocyte in steatohepatitis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Zone 3 pattern and lobular inflammation
points: Steatosis and pericellular fibrosis start around the central veins
Lobular inflammation: foci per 200x field, 0 none to 3 over 4 (NAS)

images.caption: Centrilobular (zone 3) steatosis surrounding the central veins (H&E).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Two lobular inflammatory foci (arrows) in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (H&E).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons

fields.label: Clinical context
fields.help: MASLD, MASH and MetALD need cardiometabolic and alcohol history (Rinella 2023); histology cannot separate alcohol-related from metabolic disease (RCPath G064).

reference.title: NASH CRN and SAF
reference.intro: NAS = steatosis (0-3) + lobular inflammation (0-3) + ballooning (0-2), 0-8; fibrosis is staged separately. The NAS does not replace the diagnosis of steatohepatitis (Kleiner 2005).

groups.heading: NAS components
points: Steatosis: under 5% 0; 5-33% 1; over 33-66% 2; over 66% 3
Lobular inflammation per 200x field: 0 none; 1 under 2 foci; 2 two to four; 3 over 4
Ballooning: 0 none; 1 few; 2 many or prominent

images.caption: Macrovesicular steatosis: large droplets displacing the nucleus to the periphery (H&E, x400).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 12

images.caption: Ballooned hepatocytes with rarefied cytoplasm and Mallory-Denk bodies in steatohepatitis (H&E, x200).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 15

groups.heading: NASH CRN fibrosis
points: 1a mild and 1b moderate zone 3 perisinusoidal; 1c portal or periportal only
2 perisinusoidal and portal/periportal
3 bridging; 4 cirrhosis

images.caption: Zone 3 pericellular ("chicken-wire") fibrosis in steatohepatitis (trichrome, x100).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 21

groups.heading: SAF and FLIP
points: A = ballooning (0-2) + lobular inflammation per 20x field (0 none; 1 up to 2 foci; 2 over 2)
Steatohepatitis when steatosis, ballooning and lobular inflammation are each at least 1 (Bedossa 2012)

reference.title: Liver allograft
reference.intro: Give the Banff global assessment with the RAI, then weigh the time since transplant against preservation injury, biliary or arterial complications, infection and recurrent disease (Banff 2016).

groups.heading: T-cell-mediated rejection
points: Mixed portal infiltrate with bile duct inflammation and venous subendothelial inflammation
Each RAI component scored 1-3 and summed to 9

images.caption: Acute T-cell-mediated rejection 6 days after transplant: lymphocyte (square), neutrophil (triangle), eosinophil (circle) and macrophages (hexagon) around a bile duct (B); inset, portal vein (PV) endothelial damage (H&E, x600).
images.credit: Ronca, Wootton, Milani, Cain, Front Immunol 2020, Fig 1A (cropped)

groups.heading: Central perivenulitis
points: Perivenular inflammation with hepatocyte dropout; may be the only lesion of late TCMR
Scored as venous endothelial inflammation in the RAI

images.caption: Mild central perivenulitis 51 days after transplant (H&E, x400).
images.credit: Jiang, Guo, Yang et al., J Pers Med 2023, Fig 2d (cropped)

groups.heading: Antibody-mediated rejection
points: Portal microvascular endothelial hypertrophy, capillary dilatation, microvasculitis, oedema and ductular reaction
Definite acute AMR needs the pattern, donor-specific antibody, diffuse C4d (score 3) and exclusion of other causes

images.caption: Acute antibody-mediated rejection at diagnosis: portal microvascular endothelial hypertrophy with dilated capillaries in a mixed portal infiltrate (H&E).
images.credit: Cicalese et al., Transpl Int 2024, Fig 2B (cropped)

images.caption: Intrahepatic artery with endothelial oedema and luminal narrowing in a failed allograft resected 62 days after transplant (H&E, x400).
images.credit: Jiang, Guo, Yang et al., J Pers Med 2023, Fig 1g (cropped)

groups.heading: Chronic rejection
points: Early: duct senescence, duct loss in under 50% of portal tracts; late: loss in 50% or more
Arteriolar loss, foam cell arteriopathy and perivenular fibrosis

images.caption: Chronic rejection: inflammation around the hepatic artery (white arrow) and portal vein (blue arrow), loss of the interlobular bile duct and canalicular cholestasis (H&E, x170).
images.credit: Kim et al., J Clin Med 2023, Fig 2

groups.heading: Preservation-reperfusion injury
points: Zone 3 hepatocyte swelling, apoptosis, cholestasis and sinusoidal neutrophil clusters
Usually mild and resolving within 1-2 weeks; compare with the time-zero biopsy

images.caption: Time-zero biopsy: moderate ischaemia-reperfusion injury with clusters of more than 5 neutrophils and hepatocyte dropout (x200).
images.credit: Sabry et al., Int J Hepatol 2025, Fig 4

groups.heading: Other causes
points: Recurrent disease: hepatitis B or C, AIH, PBC, PSC, steatohepatitis
Plasma cell-rich rejection: plasma cells over 30% with interface or perivenular activity
Infection (CMV inclusions, EBV) and biliary or hepatic artery complications

reference.title: Banff rejection activity index
reference.intro: Record the global assessment and the three RAI components; the grade is not derived from the RAI total (Banff 2016).

groups.heading: Portal inflammation
points: 1 mostly lymphocytic, a minority of triads, not expanding them
2 mixed infiltrate expanding most or all triads
3 marked expansion with blasts and eosinophils and periportal spillover

groups.heading: Bile duct inflammation damage
points: 1 a minority of ducts cuffed and infiltrated, mild reactive change
2 most or all ducts infiltrated, more than an occasional duct degenerate
3 most or all ducts degenerate or with focal luminal disruption

groups.heading: Venous endothelial inflammation
points: 1 subendothelial lymphocytes in some but not most venules
2 most or all venules, with or without perivenular necrosis in a minority
3 as 2 with perivenular inflammation and necrosis in the majority

reference.title: Other patterns
reference.intro: Granulomas, iron and venous outflow obstruction.

groups.heading: Granulomas
points: Epithelioid non-necrotising: sarcoidosis, PBC, drugs, hepatitis C
Necrotising: mycobacteria, fungi; negative stains do not exclude infection
Fibrin-ring: Q fever and others; lipogranulomas: steatosis

groups.heading: Iron
points: Hepatocellular grade 0-4; parenchymal iron has a periportal-to-centrilobular gradient
Mesenchymal iron is in Kupffer cells and portal macrophages; mixed patterns occur in cirrhosis

images.caption: Iron deposition (Prussian blue, x100).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 19

groups.heading: Venous outflow obstruction
points: Perivenular sinusoidal dilatation, congestion and hepatocyte loss; patchy and easily missed
Zone 3 sinusoidal dilatation alone is not specific

images.caption: Congestive hepatopathy: perivenular sinusoidal dilatation and congestion (trichrome).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

fields.label: Fibrosis
fields.help: Used when no stage is entered; a stage replaces it with the system's own words.

fields.label: Staging system
fields.help: Follows the pattern until changed: Ishak for hepatitic, NASH CRN for steatotic, none otherwise.

reference.title: Fibrosis staging
reference.intro: Choose one system; the stage words print in the microscopy and the stage in the diagnosis. Collapse after necrosis can mimic septa on reticulin; a collagen stain separates them (RCPath G064).

groups.heading: Ishak (0-6)
points: 1 some portal areas expanded; 2 most portal areas
3 occasional portal-portal bridging; 4 marked bridging including portal-central
5 marked bridging with occasional nodules (incomplete cirrhosis); 6 cirrhosis

images.caption: Fibrous expansion of a portal tract (P, arrow) without septa, as in Ishak 1-2 (haematoxylin and van Gieson).
images.credit: Boyd, Cain, Chauhan, Webb, Frontline Gastroenterol 2020, via Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Thin fibrous bridge (arrow) linking two portal tracts (P), as in Ishak 3-4 (haematoxylin and van Gieson).
images.credit: Boyd, Cain, Chauhan, Webb, Frontline Gastroenterol 2020, via Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Cirrhosis: nodules surrounded by broad fibrous septa (trichrome, x40).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 22

groups.heading: METAVIR (F0-F4) and Batts-Ludwig (0-4)
points: METAVIR: F1 portal fibrosis without septa; F2 rare septa; F3 numerous septa; F4 cirrhosis
Batts-Ludwig: 1 portal; 2 periportal or rare septa; 3 septal with distortion; 4 cirrhosis

images.caption: No fibrosis (F0): collagen (arrow) confined to the portal tract (P) in mild zone 3 steatosis (haematoxylin and van Gieson).
images.credit: Boyd, Cain, Chauhan, Webb, Frontline Gastroenterol 2020, via Wikimedia Commons

images.caption: Cirrhosis (F4): thick fibrous bands (arrows) encircling a hepatocyte nodule (haematoxylin and van Gieson).
images.credit: Boyd, Cain, Chauhan, Webb, Frontline Gastroenterol 2020, via Wikimedia Commons

groups.heading: NASH CRN (0-4)
points: 1a/1b zone 3 perisinusoidal; 1c portal/periportal
2 perisinusoidal and portal/periportal; 3 bridging; 4 cirrhosis

images.caption: Zone 3 pericellular ("chicken-wire") fibrosis in steatohepatitis (trichrome, x100).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 21

groups.heading: Stains for fibrosis
points: Collagen stain for staging: trichrome, Sirius red or van Gieson
Reticulin for collapse, plate thickness and nodular regenerative hyperplasia
Orcein or Victoria blue: elastic fibres mark long-standing septa

images.caption: Normal reticulin pattern: one- to two-cell-thick hepatocyte plates between a portal tract and a hepatic venule (reticulin).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons

reference.title: Iron (Perls)
reference.intro: Hepatocellular iron is graded 0-4; grade 2 or more raises haemochromatosis, especially without significant fibrosis (RCPath G064).

groups.heading: Scheuer grade (Searle modification)
points: 0 granules absent or barely discernible at x400
1 barely discernible at x250
2 discrete granules resolved at x100
3 discrete granules resolved at x25
4 masses visible at x10 or with the naked eye

images.caption: Iron deposition (Prussian blue, x100).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 19

groups.heading: Distribution
points: Parenchymal: biliary-pole granules with a periportal-to-centrilobular gradient
Mesenchymal: Kupffer cells and portal macrophages, no lobular gradient
Mixed: complex conditions or massive loading

fields.label: CK7
options: Ductular reaction and periportal hepatocyte expression

fields.label: CK19
options: Bile ducts in all portal tracts
fields.default: Bile ducts in all portal tracts

reference.title: Hepatitis B
reference.intro: HBsAg immunostain is more sensitive than orcein and shows membranous antigen; HBcAg is nuclear in HBeAg-positive infection (RCPath G064, Appendix B).

groups.heading: HBsAg
points: Cytoplasmic staining corresponds to ground-glass hepatocytes
Membranous staining correlates with HBV DNA
Typically negative in acute hepatitis B

images.caption: HBsAg immunostain: cytoplasmic staining of hepatocytes in chronic hepatitis B (x200).
images.credit: Choi, Int J Mol Sci 2025, Fig 5

groups.heading: Ground-glass hepatocytes
points: Finely granular eosinophilic cytoplasm
Pseudo-ground-glass change occurs with drugs

images.caption: Ground-glass hepatocytes with finely granular pale cytoplasm in chronic hepatitis B (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)
